BiblicalUsage: Zemirah appears once, in the genealogy of Benjamin, as one of the sons of Becher. He has no story of his own in Scripture — only a name in a list, a son named, a place in the tribe kept.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a name in a genealogy is not a footnote to God: every son counted, even the ones with no story attached.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
